headlines.title: Hormuz shipping traffic falls to single digits, data shows - Reuters
headlines.summary: Hormuz traffic in single digits is the tape-screaming headline of the week — that strait moves roughly 20% of the world's seaborne oil, and near-zero throughput is a five-alarm fire for energy markets, inflation, and every sector that runs on diesel. This feeds directly into the $6-a-gallon diesel record, the IEA's demand-slash, the ECB rate hike, and the 30-year Treasury yield pushing 5.3% — it's the root cause of the whole market selloff. Airlines, truckers, chemicals, and anyone with a supply chain feels this in the gut.

headlines.title: Stocks and Treasuries Regain Ground Ahead of CPI: Markets Wrap
headlines.summary: Friday's CPI print is the single most time-sensitive data point on the calendar right now — with the 10-year yield knocking on 5% and the Fed meeting next week, a hot number could tip the scales toward another hike and send the whole tape back down hard. The market is already on its worst weekly stretch since June, so this number lands on a bruised tape with no margin for error. Every sector from tech to housing to private credit is watching that 8:30 print like a hawk.

headlines.title: Oracle jumps 6% after reporting 30% revenue growth fueled by AI cloud demand
headlines.summary: Oracle dropping a 30% revenue growth quarter with cloud infrastructure up 121% is a genuine shot in the arm for the AI trade at a moment when the broader market desperately needs good news. This lifts sentiment across the hyperscaler and AI infrastructure complex — think NVDA, MSFT, AMD — and confirms enterprise AI spending is real, not vaporware. On a week when oil and rates have been beating the market senseless, Oracle's beat is the one bright spot keeping tech bulls from throwing in the towel.
